question:
Why does hydrogen iodide (HI) have a higher boiling point than hydrogen bromide (HBr)?

[Atomic numbers: bromine = 35 iodine = 53]

choices.A: The iodide ions in HI are larger than the bromide ions in HBr.
choices.B: The H–I covalent bond is stronger than the H–Br covalent bond.
choices.C: There are hydrogen bonds between HI molecules but not between HBr molecules.
choices.D: The permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces between HI molecules are stronger than those between HBr molecules.
choices.E: The induced dipole-induced dipole (dispersion) forces between HI molecules are stronger than those between HBr molecules.
